FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: nikuman
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a {0_adj} bun steamed soft, filled with minced {1_plur} and {2_plur}, so white and so yielding that you know it by touch. Sold in winter over the counter of the night shops.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: udon
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: thick, soft noodles kneaded underfoot beneath a cloth, in a clear {1_adj} broth. The texture matters more than the taste, and it is deliberate.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: soba
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: grey {0_adj} noodles, served cold on a rack with a {1_adj} sauce apart. The cooking water is drunk at the end, let down in what is left of the sauce.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: agedashi dofu
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: cubes of {0_adj} tofu rolled in starch and fried, set into a warm {1_adj} broth. The crust holds just long enough to reach the table.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: oyakodon
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} and {2_coll} barely set together in a sweet-salt broth and poured over {0_coll}. The name means parent and child; nobody has ever claimed it was delicate.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gyudon
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} shaved paper-thin and stewed with {2_plur} in a sweet broth, served over {0_coll}. The fastest meal it is possible to eat sitting down.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: katsudon
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a {1_adj} chop crumbed and fried, then dipped back into a {2_adj} broth that softens the coating on purpose, laid over {0_coll}. Eaten the night before an examination: katsu also means to win.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: onigiri
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} pressed into a triangle with salted, wetted hands, filled with {2_adj} and belted with {1_plur}. It keeps a whole day in a pocket.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: okonomiyaki
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a thick pancake in which shredded {1_coll} barely holds together with {0_plur} and {2_plur}, cooked on the plate in front of you. The name means grilled as you like it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: chawanmushi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a savoury {0_adj} custard steamed gently, so barely set that it is eaten with a spoon, with {1_coll} and {2_coll} hidden at the bottom. Too hot and it riddles itself with bubbles and is spoiled.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: nikujaga
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} stewed with {2_plur} and sugar under a dropped lid, until there is almost no liquid left. The dish people name when they talk about their mother's cooking.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: chikuzenni
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} cut on the bias, seared in oil then stewed dry with {2_coll}, until the liquid has vanished entirely into the vegetables.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: nanbanzuke
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} fried and then marinated hot in a sweetened vinegar with {1_plur} and {2_plur}. Nanban means the Portuguese, to whom the method is owed.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tonjiru
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a soup of fermented {2_adj} loaded with {0_adj} and roots, {1_coll} among them. More sustaining than an ordinary miso soup, and served when it freezes.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: karaage
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} marinated in {1_plur} and {2_plur}, rolled in starch and fried twice over. The starch gives a thin, brittle crust, very unlike a crumb coating.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: korokke
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a mash of {0_adj} mixed with minced {2_plur}, crumbed in coarse breadcrumbs and fried. A distant descendant of the French croquette, which arrived by boat last century.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: chirashi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: vinegared {0_coll} spread over the bottom of a bowl and scattered — which is what the name says — with raw {1_plur} in slices and ribbons of omelette. All the difficulty of sushi, without the gesture of sushi.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: ochazuke
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: scalding {1_coll} poured over cold rice, with {2_coll} crumbled into it. The meal at the end of an evening, or at the end of the leftovers — the two often come to the same thing.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: dorayaki
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: two small thick pancakes made with {2_plur} and honey, closed over a sweet {1_adj} paste. The name comes from the gong they imitate.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: anmitsu
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: cubes of {1_adj} jelly — firm, barely sweetened — with a {0_adj} paste and a black {2_adj} syrup poured at the table. The summer dessert, served iced.
